judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scope clause defines "Securities" as "securities or other assets," a deliberately open-ended phrase whose outer boundary is not fixed by any enumeration. Otherwise the applicability language is standard and non-operative in any contested sense.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Paragraph 11(v) and 11(a)'s automatic deemed exercise, and nothing in Annex III or V contradicts it. No competing definition of insolvency appears anywhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cross-reference is rendered "Paragraph 4(~) hencrA", an unreadable citation, though the intended reference to 4(a) is recoverable from Paragraph 4(a)'s own parenthetical definition. The term itself is otherwise purely referential.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line pointer definition with no substantive content and nothing capable of two meanings. Purely referential.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 3(b) supplies the referenced meaning and Annex VI paragraph 3 adapts it for Buy/Sell Back Transactions without contradiction. No competing definition exists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference to Paragraph 4(a) with no independent wording to construe. Nothing ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 4(a) defines the term parenthetically, and Annex III paragraph 7 supplies a currency-conversion rule for its calculation without conflict. Consistent throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Another one-line pointer definition with no substantive content. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 4(b) supplies the meaning and Annex III paragraph 7 governs conversion, with no competing usage. Coherent with the rest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The fallback — "the deadline for such purposes established in accordance with market practice" — is an unfixed external standard whose content two parties could readily dispute. That is a nameable vagueness in the operative default.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No Margin Notice Deadline is fixed in Annex I or Annex II, so the vague fallback is the operative rule for Paragraph 4(c) and Annex V paragraph 2(e). The gap is a drafting omission rather than a contradiction of another clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]he price ... obtained from a generally recognized source agreed to by the parties or the most recent closing bid quotation from such a source ... (unless contrary to market practice for such Securities)" stacks three indeterminate standards, and for illiquid mortgage collateral there may be no such source at all. Each of "generally recognized source," "closing bid quotation" and "market practice" is separately contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives Paragraph 4(a)'s Margin Deficit, and sits against Paragraph 11(d)'s acknowledgment that the Securities "are instruments traded in a recognized market" and that in the absence of such a source the nondefaulting party may pick one "in its sole discretion" — a real tension about who fixes value and by what measure. Annex I neither defines a pricing source nor disapplies that acknowledgment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise daily-accrual formula with explicit inclusive/exclusive date conventions and a reduction for amounts already paid. Nothing evaluative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex VI paragraph 4(b) creates a parallel Sell Back Differential for Buy/Sell Back Transactions without disturbing this definition. Consistent with 2(r) and 11(f).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definition that leaves the rate itself to be agreed elsewhere; the wording is definite even if the number is not supplied here. Nothing ambiguous in the phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 3(b)(iv) requires the Pricing Rate or Repurchase Price in the Confirmation and Annex VI paragraph 5 requires it recorded, so the blank is filled by trade documents. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An objectively verifiable published rate with an averaging tie-breaker; little room for two readings. The source is named specifically.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex III paragraph 1(b) expressly overrides this definition for International Transactions with LIBOR plus an unspecified spread, which is a stated override rather than a contradiction. Paragraph 11(h) uses the term as defined.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-clause date definition with no evaluative content. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex V's "Forward Transaction" definition keys off the same date and Paragraph 11(a) cancels transactions whose Purchase Date has not occurred, all consistently. No friction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is mechanical: an opening price adjusted up and down by identified cash movements. "[E]xcept where Buyer and Seller agree otherwise" is an ordinary opt-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Paragraphs 4(a), 4(b) and 5(ii), and Annex I paragraph 3 disapplies the 5(ii) route entirely, so one limb of the adjustment can never operate. That is a redundancy rather than a genuine inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is inclusive and exclusive in express terms, with no vague boundary word. It is drafted with care.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 4(a) permits margin to be met with cash as well as Additional Purchased Securities, yet only the latter become Purchased Securities, so cash margin sits outside the defined collateral pool that Paragraph 6 pledges and 11(d)(i) liquidates. That gap is arguable but Paragraph 12's set-off and netting language largely closes it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A date definition expressly extended to dates fixed under Paragraphs 3(c) and 11. Clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex III paragraph 6(c) also nominates a Repurchase Date on a Tax Event, which this definition's "including" language accommodates without listing it. A minor incompleteness, not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is garbled at the crucial point ("the SUlliR)f the Purchase Price and the Price Differential"), though the intended "sum of" is plain from context. The substance is a formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex VI paragraph 10 directs that all references to Repurchase Price be read as "Repurchase Price or the Sell Back Price, as the case may be," and Paragraph 11(f) caps it; both are compatible glosses. No contradiction identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mirror-image arithmetical definition with no evaluative term. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in Paragraph 4(b) and Annex III paragraph 7, both consistently. No competing provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mirrors 2(d) with the same mechanical fallback formula and no vague standard of its own. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex VII paragraph 2 addresses only Buyer's Margin Percentage even in the sentence about a Fund acting as Seller, leaving Seller's Margin Percentage untouched here. That oddity lies in Annex VII rather than in this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permitting an agreement to be "made orally" is clear, if commercially risky; there is no ambiguous term to name. The delivery-versus-payment sentence is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Oral formation sits against Paragraph 3(b)'s "conclusive evidence" rule and Paragraph 17's requirement that modifications be in writing, which can be harmonised but leaves scope for argument about what was agreed. Annex IV paragraph 2(b) also assumes oral agreement, confirming the design.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]onclusive evidence ... unless ... specific objection is made promptly" turns on the undefined word "promptly," and "any additional terms or conditions ... not inconsistent with this Agreement" invites argument about what counts as inconsistent. Both are nameable soft edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This clause makes the Agreement prevail over a Confirmation, while Annex I paragraph 2, Annex VI paragraph 1 and Annex VII all make their own annexes prevail over the Agreement, producing a layered priority scheme with no single ordering rule. A Confirmation term overridden by the Agreement but blessed by an annex is a real ordering puzzle.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[N]o later than such time as is customary in accordance with market practice" imports an unfixed external standard into the demand mechanic. That is a specific vagueness a court could be asked to fill.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with 2(q) and Paragraph 11(a)'s deemed acceleration, and nothing in the annexes contradicts the demand mechanism. Annex VI paragraph 6 supplies a parallel termination rule for Buy/Sell Back Transactions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The margin trigger rests entirely on "aggregate Market Value," and the collateral must be "additional Securities reasonably acceptable to Buyer" — both indeterminate standards controlled in practice by one side. judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends directly on the 2(j) Market Value definition and is enforced through Paragraph 11(iii), which makes non-compliance an immediate Event of Default without notice or cure even though the margin right is itself permissive ("Buyer may by notice"). Annex I fixes no threshold under 4(e) or deadline under 2(i), so the mechanism runs on the bare default standards.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mirror provision uses the same "Market Value" standard but is otherwise mechanical, and the return is at Buyer's option as to form. Less contestable than 4(a) because it is the Seller's claim.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 2(s)/2(t) and Paragraph 11(iii) treats failure to comply as an Event of Default for either side; Annex I neither sets a threshold nor disapplies it. No direct conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear same-day/next-day timing rule keyed to a defined deadline; "close of business in the relevant market" is the only soft term. Otherwise precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its operation depends on the 2(i) Margin Notice Deadline, which is undefined here and defaults to market practice, and Annex V paragraph 2(e) mirrors it. Dependent but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short attribution rule that simply defers to later agreement, with no ambiguous term. It does, however, provide no default if the parties never agree.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The silence matters for Paragraph 2(o)'s Purchase Price adjustments and 4(f)'s transaction-by-transaction election, but nothing contradicts it. A gap rather than a clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure enabling provision requiring a further agreement on a threshold; nothing operative is left vague. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I contains no such threshold agreement, so this option was simply never exercised. No conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Another enabling provision permitting a per-Transaction election, drafted in plain terms. No vague operative standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex IV paragraph 4(b)(iii) and Annex VII paragraph 1(a) prescribe transaction-by-transaction or per-Fund margining in their own contexts, which supplement rather than contradict this election. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]s Buyer shall reasonably determine in its discretion" pairs a reasonableness standard with unfettered discretion, and the reach of "all Income" depends on the broad 2(f) definition including principal. Both are nameable soft spots.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I paragraph 3 removes Buyer's election by mandating the 5(i) transfer and forbidding the 5(ii) application, while Annex VI paragraph 9 disapplies Paragraph 5 altogether and reverses the payment direction — three overlapping regimes for the same subject. Paragraph 11(iv) then makes failure to comply an Event of Default only after notice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is expressly conditional and protective ("in the event any such Transactions are deemed to be loans"), which is clear drafting, though the sale/loan characterisation it hedges is the perennially contested issue in repo. The words themselves are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Paragraph 8's statement that "[a]ll of Seller's interest in the Purchased Securities shall pass to Buyer on the Purchase Date" and Paragraph 19's bankruptcy-characterisation recitals, which pull toward true sale; the pledge language is the deliberate counterweight. Reconcilable as a fallback, but the tension is genuine.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-limb transfer-mechanics provision with a mutual-agreement catch-all; the limbs are alternatives and the standard ("reasonably request") is conventional. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex III paragraph 2 restates it for International Securities and Annex VII paragraph 5 routes Fund transfers through a Custodian, both consistently. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "To the extent required by applicable law" makes the segregation duty contingent on an unspecified external body of law, and the same paragraph both passes all of Seller's interest to Buyer and preserves Buyer's return obligations. That combination is workable but not self-evident.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reads against Paragraph 6's deemed pledge and Paragraph 9(b)'s deemed consent to substitution where Seller retains custody, plus the bracketed Required Disclosure that follows. The pieces are meant to fit but the title/pledge duality is the same tension flagged at Paragraph 6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The disclosure retains unselected alternatives — "[will]* [may]**", "[its clearing bank]* [third parties]**", "[the clearing]* [any]** lien" — so the operative words were never chosen. That is a mechanical defect visible on the face of the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states flatly that Seller "is not permitted to substitute" absent a grant, while Paragraph 9(b) deems Buyer to have consented to substitution in exactly the retained-custody case and Annex I paragraph 4 adds a further substitution right. judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short consensual substitution mechanic with no vague term; substitution requires agreement and acceptance. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 9(b) deems that agreement given in retained-custody transactions, and Annex I paragraph 4 bolts on new subparagraphs (c) and (d) giving Seller a unilateral notice right subject to Buyer's veto — three overlapping substitution regimes. They can be sequenced, but the interaction requires work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deemed-consent rule is stated plainly, with the only qualification being an equal-Market-Value proviso that imports the contested 2(j) standard. "[S]ubstantially the same" does not appear here, so the clause is fairly tight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts the bracketed Required Disclosure's statement that Seller "is not permitted to substitute" unless Buyer grants the right — though that disclosure arguably is the grant. Annex I paragraph 4's new 9(c) presupposes cases where no existing substitution right exists, which sits awkwardly with this deemed grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional five-limb representation list, each limb specific and closing with a broad but familiar no-violation clause. Nothing genuinely indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I paragraph 5, Annex IV paragraph 1 and Annex VII paragraph 4 add further representations expressly "in addition to" this paragraph. Additive, not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 4 confers rights in permissive terms ("may by notice require"), so what constitutes non-compliance is fixed only by reading 4(c)'s timing rule together with this limb; Annex III paragraph 8(a) and Annex V paragraph 4(a) add further Events of Default with a notice requirement. judgments.reasoning_cat1: The automatic deemed exercise on an Act of Insolvency, coupled with an obligation to give notice "as promptly as practicable" except in that case, is clearly drafted though "practicable" is soft. The cancellation carve-out for un-started Transactions is explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with 2(q), 11(b)-(d) and Annex V paragraph 4(b), all of which key off "the option referred to in subparagraph (a)." No inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-limb acceleration and application rule stated in definite terms, with the only imported standard being the Repurchase Price. Little to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex VI paragraph 11 rewrites "Repurchase Prices" here to include Sell Back Prices, and Paragraph 5(B) suspends Income remittance on Seller default consistently with limb (ii). Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional transfer-of-title rule triggered by tender; clear in structure though "tender" is undefined. Little genuine ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 11(d)(ii) and 11(e)'s replacement-cost remedy, and Paragraph 11(f) caps the Repurchase Price in exactly this configuration. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs against the 2(j) Market Value definition and against the acknowledgment immediately following that the Securities "are instruments traded in a recognized market" and that the nondefaulting party may pick the pricing source "in its sole discretion," which arguably neuters the commercial-reasonableness limit. judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts directly against 11(d)(i)'s alternative of "otherwise in a commercially reasonable manner" (which presupposes no recognized market) and against 2(j)'s requirement of a source "agreed to by the parties." judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific measure of damages (excess of replacement price over Repurchase Price) plus a cross-reference; the text is precise. The garbled OCR does not obscure the meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pairs with 11(d)(ii), 11(f)'s cap and 11(g)'s general damages heads without duplication problems. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence cap keyed to the date of exercise; unambiguous in operation, though a page header is spliced into the OCR text. Nothing evaluative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies 11(b), 11(e) and Annex VI paragraph 11's Sell Back Price gloss consistently, and applies only where the defaulting party is Buyer. No inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Annex I paragraph 4's new 9(d), which imposes similar replacement and hedge costs on substitution or termination, and with Annex III paragraph 6(e)'s bar on consequential loss for Tax Event terminations. judgments.reasoning_cat1: A default-interest clause with a clearly specified rate (greater of Pricing Rate or Prime Rate) and defined running period. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relies on 2(m) Prime Rate, which Annex III paragraph 1(b) replaces with LIBOR plus spread for International Transactions; that is an express override. No genuine clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short cumulative-remedies saving clause; broad but of a familiar and settled kind. Nothing specific to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex IV paragraph 3 limits the other party's remedies against an Agent, and Annex VII paragraph 1(c) bars cross-Fund set-off, both cutting against an unlimited reading of this clause. Those limits are expressly stated, so the hierarchy is workable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carefully drafted single-agreement, set-off and netting provision with three enumerated consequences and no evaluative term. Its cross-default effect is stated squarely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notices "may be given" by any of several methods and "may be made orally, to be confirmed promptly in writing," which leaves both the permissive/mandatory character and the effect of an unconfirmed oral notice open. "[P]romptly" is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It points to addresses "specified in Annex II," a page of names and addresses that distinguishes legal notices from operational contacts without saying which controls margin calls under Paragraph 4. judgments.reasoning_cat1: The supersession is limited to prior agreements "containing general terms and conditions for repurchase transactions," a bounded phrase rather than a full merger clause, and severability is stated plainly. The limit is deliberate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because it is not a complete integration clause, Confirmations under Paragraph 3(b) and the several annexes remain operative alongside it, which is how the instrument is designed. No contradiction identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assignment is barred and any purported assignment is "null and void," and termination is by written notice with outstanding Transactions preserved — all definite. Nothing evaluative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subparagraph (b) carves out assignment of Paragraph 11 sums, and Annex IV paragraph 5's deeming of Principals as parties is a different mechanism; neither contradicts this. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow carve-out permitting dealings with sums payable under Paragraph 11; the boundary between assigning a "sum payable" and assigning "rights and obligations" under (a) is fine but conventional. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly qualifies 15(a) and interacts with Paragraph 12's netting of amounts across Transactions, which could complicate an assignment of a single Paragraph 11 claim. That interaction is subtle rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line New York choice of law excluding renvoi; about as definite as drafting gets. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I paragraph 6's non-exclusive submission to New York courts is consistent with it, and no annex selects a different law. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause requires modifications and consents to be "in writing and duly executed by both of the parties," which is clear, and expressly preserves late margin calls. "[I]mplied waiver" is mentioned but the operative rule is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Paragraph 3(a)'s oral Transaction agreements, Paragraph 13's oral notices, and the many annex provisions turning on what the parties "may agree" without formality, so whether an oral trade agreement is a prohibited modification is arguable. Annex V paragraph 5 restates the no-waiver rule for Forward Collateral consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A notification and representation requirement for ERISA plan assets, stated in specific terms with an express right not to proceed. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex IV paragraph 4(d) separately dictates how ERISA plan Transactions are treated when an Agent is involved, supplementing rather than contradicting this. No clash located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It makes a Transaction proceed "only if" Seller furnishes financial statements, while opening "[s]ubject to the last sentence of subparagraph (a)" — a mandatory condition qualified by a discretionary one. That interlock is slightly awkward but comprehensible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The qualification points back to 18(a)'s statement that the other party "may proceed in reliance thereon but shall not be required so to proceed," and Annex VII paragraph 4 imposes a parallel financial-information duty. Reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A deemed representation of no "material adverse change" plus an ongoing delivery undertaking; "material adverse change" is soft but ubiquitous and here bounded by non-disclosure. Otherwise specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A breach feeds Paragraph 11(vi)'s Event of Default for incorrect representations, and Annex VII paragraph 4 duplicates the information duty for Funds. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recognition is immediately qualified by "except insofar as the type of Securities ... or the term ... would render such definition inapplicable," a self-cancelling proviso that leaves the characterisation of any given trade unresolved. Naming what falls outside the statutory definitions is exactly the open question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It points toward true-sale/safe-harbour characterisation while Paragraph 6 provides a deemed pledge if Transactions are "deemed to be loans," so the instrument hedges both ways. That is deliberate belt-and-braces drafting, but the two do point in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text cites "Sections 555 and 559 of Title II of the United States Code," plainly a mis-rendering of Title 11, which is a mechanical citation error on the face of the provision. The substance is otherwise a straightforward acknowledgment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces the Paragraph 11 remedies and 19(a)'s characterisation, and Paragraph 6's fallback pledge does not contradict it. Consistent in substance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional statutory characterisation with an express carve-out for inapplicable asset types; definite as far as it goes. Nothing evaluative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Neither party here is an insured depository institution, so the clause is inert; Annex I paragraph 5's FDICIA representations occupy adjacent ground without conflict. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A netting-contract characterisation with a stated exception where a party is not a "financial institution"; the exception is precise. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I paragraph 5 has the parties represent that they are financial institutions or meet Regulation EE tests, which supports rather than undercuts this. Paragraph 12 supplies the netting mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure regulatory disclosure that a third party "has taken the position"; it creates no obligation and states no standard. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 20(b) and (c) and with Paragraph 19's characterisations without friction. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat statement of statutory non-protection, specific as to the registration category. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 20(a) and (c) and with Paragraph 2(a)'s reference to SIPA proceedings. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short disclosure that repo funds are not insured deposits; definite and non-operative. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aligns with 19(c)'s insured-depository-institution language and creates no obligation that could clash. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is a checklist of annexes with no election marks preserved in the text, so which annexes were in fact adopted is not evident from the words. The garbled rendering ("this Annex land Annex JL") compounds the difficulty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read literally it makes Annex IV (party acting as agent), Annex VI (buy/sell back) and Annex VII (registered investment companies, with a wholly blank Schedule VII.A and a blank margin percentage) part of a two-party principal-to-principal agreement, and Annex VII even names Barclays and unnamed Funds rather than Thornburg. judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ny inconsistency" is an undefined trigger, and the clause does not say whether it covers mere supplementation or only true contradiction. That is a nameable soft edge in a priority rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes Annex I govern over the Agreement, while Paragraph 3(b) makes the Agreement prevail over Confirmations and Annex VI paragraph 1 and Annex VII each make their own annex prevail over "any other term of the Agreement" — with no tie-breaker among the annexes themselves. The competing precedence clauses cannot all be applied in a case where two annexes disagree.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading reads "Purchase Price Maintenance" but the text is entirely about Income payment treatment, a mismatch between label and content. The operative sentence itself is otherwise clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It turns on "substantially the same Securities," an undefined standard of equivalence, and closes with the obligation that Buyer "shall offer Seller the right to terminate" without saying on what terms or by when. Both are specific indeterminacies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends Paragraph 9, which already requires Buyer's agreement, and overlaps with 9(b)'s deemed acceptance in retained-custody trades and with the Required Disclosure's statement that substitution is not permitted. The layering creates real questions about which regime governs a given substitution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Costs are "solely determined and calculated by Buyer in good faith," and the recoverable heads include an open-ended "loss incurred by Buyer directly arising or resulting from" the substitution — one-sided drafting with a self-judging measure. "[A]ctual cost" and "loss" both invite dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It imposes replacement and hedge costs on Seller for exercising a right the same amendment grants, and duplicates the damages heads in Paragraph 11(g) which apply only on default. The overlap of default-style damages with a non-default event is noticeable but not a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An either/or representation tied to defined regulatory tests; the second limb incorporates Regulation EE's quantitative thresholds rather than leaving a standard at large. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports Paragraph 19(d)'s netting-contract characterisation and adds to Paragraph 10 as stated. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Submission is "non-exclusive" yet stated to be "solely for the purpose of" enforcement suits, a combination that does not clearly answer whether other forums remain open for other claims. Mildly contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Paragraph 16's New York choice of law and nothing elsewhere selects another forum. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but conventional immunity waiver with an enumerated list of processes and a general closing phrase. Little practical indeterminacy between two US commercial parties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements Annex I paragraph 6 and conflicts with nothing else in the instrument. Inert here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bundle of definitions, most precise, though "International Security" sweeps in any Security "capable of being cleared through a clearing facility outside the United States" — a very wide and arguable test. That breadth could capture ordinary domestic securities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The clause defines "Business Day" "[f]or purposes of the Agreement," yet every limb is framed only for International Transactions, leaving the many domestic "business day" references in Paragraphs 4(c), 11 and Annex V without a definition. That is a genuine gap created by the annex's own framing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It redefines "Prime Rate" as "LIBOR plus a spread, as may be specified" — if no spread is ever specified, the rate is indeterminate, and it is odd to call a LIBOR-based rate the Prime Rate. The open spread is a nameable gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly overrides Paragraph 2(m) for International Transactions and feeds Paragraph 11(h)'s default interest, so a defaulting party's interest rate depends on a term the contract never fixes. The override is stated, which reduces the incoherence to a gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four alternative transfer methods closing with mutual agreement; each limb is concrete. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels Paragraph 7 for International Securities without displacing it in terms, but the two lists are alternatives rather than rivals. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line default currency rule subject to contrary agreement. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Contractual Currency definition in Annex III paragraph 1(a) supplies the referent and 3(b)-(d) handle deviations. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The discharge rule turns on what the payee "may, consistent with normal banking procedures, purchase" — a market-practice standard, though a familiar one in currency-indemnity drafting. Modest softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 3(c)'s shortfall obligation and 3(d)'s refund duty as an integrated scheme. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard judgment-currency indemnity expressed as a separate and independent obligation; long but precise. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out for a nondefaulting party mirrors 3(d) and Annex III paragraph 8(b)'s conversion remedy. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short refund obligation with a defined exception; "promptly" is the only soft word. Otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors 3(c) and coexists with Annex III paragraph 8(b). No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short rule directing notices to follow Paragraph 13 and be in English. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It incorporates Paragraph 13, which itself permits oral notices, so an oral notice "in the English language" is coherent. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ll similar costs" is a general catch-all appended to two specific tax types, so its outer reach is uncertain. That is the classic general-after-specific structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It allocates all transfer costs to Seller regardless of who is defaulting, which sits alongside but does not contradict Paragraph 11(g)'s expense allocation. No clash identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso refers to "Paragraphs 5 and 6" without saying whether those are paragraphs of Annex III or of the Agreement, and the connection test ("other than the mere receipt of payment") is evaluative. The ambiguous cross-reference is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly coordinates with Paragraph 5 of the Agreement on Income, and Annex I paragraph 3's mandated Income transfer is unaffected. Workable together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A documentary cooperation duty qualified only by "reasonably requested"; conventional and narrow. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the condition for 5(b)(iv)'s cut-back of gross-up and is consistent with it. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[K]nown or reasonably known to it" is slightly odd phrasing but the duty is specific to the certificates already given. Minor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with 5(b)(ii) and (iv) and with the Paragraph 6 Change of Tax Law carve-out. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise cut-back of the gross-up keyed to identified breaches. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies 5(b)(i) expressly and does not disturb Paragraph 5 of the Agreement. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger requires that a Change of Tax Law "has or will, in the notifying party's reasonable opinion, have a material adverse effect," combining a self-judged opinion with an undefined materiality standard. Both terms are contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the gateway to 6(b)-(f) and interacts sensibly with the tax gross-up in paragraph 5, as 6(f) confirms. No inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]uitably qualified adviser" is loose but the obligation is narrow and conditional on request. Limited exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports 6(a) and does not affect any other provision. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A termination right with a specific 30-day minimum notice and a defined mechanism (nominating a Repurchase Date). Precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies an additional Repurchase Date not listed in Paragraph 2(q)'s "including" clause, which is inclusive rather than exhaustive. Minor incompleteness only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The counter-notice creates a deemed indemnity "against the adverse effect ... so far as it relates to the relevant International Transaction," a measure of loss left undefined. That scope phrase is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides 6(c)'s termination right and preserves the original Repurchase Date, an intended interlock. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An indemnity for "reasonable legal and other professional expenses" with an express bar on consequential loss; both limbs are conventional. Modest softness in "consequential."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The bar on consequential loss for Tax Event terminations contrasts with Paragraph 11(g)'s broad damages on default, but the two address different events. Reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[W]here appropriate" is an open standard governing when a gross-up obligation can trigger the Tax Event machinery. Small but nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly reconciles Annex III paragraphs 5 and 6, which is the opposite of a conflict. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line conversion rule using the defined Spot Rate. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplements Paragraph 4's calculations for non-Base-Currency sums without displacing them. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An additional Event of Default for failure to perform "any covenant or obligation" under the annex, with an illustrative "including, without limitation" example — broad, but with a one-business-day notice built in. The breadth is stated, not hidden.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It differs from Paragraph 11(iii)'s no-notice treatment of margin failures, an asymmetry that runs through the instrument (compare Annex V paragraph 4(a)). Different triggers rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A currency-conversion and offset remedy exercisable "at any time at its option" at the defined Spot Rate. Definite in mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds to Paragraph 11 remedies and complements Paragraph 12's netting; Annex IV paragraph 3(b) limits set-off only against an Agent. No conflict here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A scope recital identifying Agent and Principal; definitional and non-operative. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I paragraph 1 makes this annex applicable although Paragraph 10(ii) has each party represent it acts as principal unless otherwise agreed in writing in advance, so an agency annex sits over a principal-to-principal deal. The annex is conditional on agency arising, which defuses much of the tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A continuing authority representation stated in specific terms. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It builds on Paragraph 10 as stated and its breach feeds Paragraph 11(vi); Annex IV paragraph 3 makes its truth the condition of the liability limit. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The other party may reject a Principal it determines "in its sole discretion" is unacceptable, and the unwind obligations are elaborate with a proviso preserving Price Differential "or other amounts" — a broad residual phrase. The sole-discretion rescission right is one-sidedly drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes Paragraph 3(a)'s oral agreements and interacts with Annex IV paragraphs 4(b) and 4(c) on notice content, all consistently. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The limitation is conditioned on representations being "true and correct in all material respects" and on compliance with the annex; materiality is soft but the consequences are specific. Reasonably tight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts down the set-off rights conferred by Paragraph 12(ii) and the cumulative remedies preserved by Paragraph 11(i), but does so expressly and only as against an Agent. A stated qualification rather than a clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A binary election with an express default if no written election is made; the drafting anticipates its own gap. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subparagraphs (b), (c) and (d) work out both branches consistently, and Annex VII paragraph 1 applies a similar per-Fund logic. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated consequences of the separate-Principals election, each specific, with a parenthetical allowing a Principal-by-Principal margin alternative. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It modifies how Paragraph 4 margining and Paragraph 11 remedies operate and implicitly qualifies Paragraph 12's single-agreement netting, though it says so expressly by deeming separate Agreements. Workable together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The single-Principal branch is stated in three concrete consequences, qualified only by "any greater requirement imposed by applicable law." Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aggregates margin across Principals, which sits against Annex VII paragraph 1(a)'s insistence on per-Fund application and 4(d)'s ERISA carve-out; those are expressly reconciled by their own "notwithstanding" language. No live conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A "notwithstanding any other provision" override with a single, precisely stated consequence for ERISA plans. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides 4(a)'s election and 4(c)'s aggregation in ERISA cases and complements Paragraph 18's plan-asset regime. Expressly reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming machinery is elaborate and turns on constructions "subject to the provisions of this Annex IV," leaving how far Agent is bound as a "party" to be worked out. The parenthetical making an Act of Insolvency of Agent an Event of Default by Seller or Buyer is a strong deeming rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Deeming Agent a "party" with a Principal's Event of Default consequences pulls against Annex IV paragraph 3, which says Agent's obligations do not include a guarantee of its Principals' performance and bars set-off against Agent's own transactions. The two can be reconciled only by reading paragraph 3 as the controlling qualification, which paragraph 5 acknowledges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Forward Exposure" is "the amount of loss a party would incur upon canceling ... and entering into a replacement transaction, determined in accordance with market practice or as otherwise agreed" — a hypothetical loss measured by an unfixed external standard. That is a nameable vagueness at the heart of the annex.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The chain of definitions feeds Annex V paragraph 2's margining and depends on the Agreement's "Market Value," inheriting whatever indeterminacy that carries. Otherwise consistent with Paragraph 4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger rests on Net Unsecured Forward Exposure and on collateral "reasonably acceptable" to the calling party, both evaluative but structurally parallel to Paragraph 4(a). Moderately soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states that these rights are "in addition to" Paragraph 4(a) and (b), so overlapping calls on the same Transaction are contemplated rather than prohibited. The interaction with Paragraph 4 is expressly addressed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure enabling threshold provision requiring further agreement. Nothing operative to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No such agreement appears in Annex I, so the option was never exercised. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enabling election for per-Transaction calculation, mirroring Paragraph 4(f). Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Paragraph 4(f) and Annex IV paragraph 4(b)(iii). No clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two enabling alternatives for initial and minimum transfer amounts, each requiring an agreed figure. Nothing indeterminate in the wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relies on the Margin Notice Deadline, which the parties never fixed, so the timing runs on the 2(i) market-practice default. A dependency rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A same-day/next-day timing rule identical in structure to Paragraph 4(c). Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the undefined Margin Notice Deadline and mirrors Paragraph 4(c) consistently. No inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A return obligation on settlement subject to a clear proviso preventing the creation of exposure. Precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with Annex V paragraph 2(a) and with the Purchase Date definition in Paragraph 2(n). Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision uses "Pledgor (as defined below)" and "Pledgee (as defined below)" although those terms are first defined in the following paragraph — a forward reference that is untidy but recoverable. The substitution mechanic itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels Paragraph 9(a) for Forward Collateral without displacing it, and no annex contradicts it. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad pledge and set-off grant covering Forward Collateral "and any other cash, Securities or property" transferred or due — the sweep-in of anything "due from Pledgee to Pledgor" is wide but expressly stated. Little hidden ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly "[i]n addition to the rights granted ... under Paragraph 6," which itself only creates a deemed pledge if Transactions are recharacterised as loans; the two grants operate at different levels. No contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An expansive rehypothecation right with a proviso preserving return obligations; the drafting is explicit about the excess amounts and longer periods it permits. Clear if aggressive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Paragraph 8's treatment of Purchased Securities and preserves the transfer duties under Annex V paragraph 2 and Paragraph 11. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An additional Event of Default triggered only after one business day's notice, covering "any covenant or obligation" under the annex. Broad but plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its notice requirement differs from Paragraph 11(iii)'s immediate default for margin failures, the same asymmetry seen in Annex III paragraph 8(a). Different triggers, not contradictory ones.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It repeats the same self-judging standards as Paragraph 11(d) — "commercially reasonable manner," prices the nondefaulting party "may reasonably deem satisfactory," "sole discretion" pricing sources — and again stipulates that all Forward Collateral "are instruments traded in a recognized market." Those stipulations are contestable in the same way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly additional to Paragraphs 11 and 12 and keys off Paragraph 11(a)'s option, but its recognized-market stipulation cuts against its own commercially-reasonable alternative and against Paragraph 2(j)'s agreed-source valuation. The tension parallels the one in the main body.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line non-waiver saving clause mirroring Paragraph 17's last sentence. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly operates "[w]ithout limitation of the provisions of Paragraph 17" and matches it. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A scope recital identifying the annex, the date and the parties; wholly definitional. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is made applicable by Annex I paragraph 1 even though no Buy/Sell Back Transactions are evidenced, which is a checkbox oddity rather than an inconsistency. The substantive precedence rule sits in paragraph 1 of the annex.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blunt precedence rule using the undefined trigger "any conflict"; the wording itself is short and plain. Limited intrinsic ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes Annex VI prevail over "any other term of the Agreement," while Annex I paragraph 2 makes Annex I govern over the Agreement and Annex VII claims the same primacy — three unranked precedence clauses with no tie-breaker. Where Annex I paragraph 3 and Annex VI paragraph 9 give opposite Income rules, this circularity actually bites.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mandatory classification requirement stated in one line; the consequence of failing to classify is not addressed. That silence is a gap rather than an ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires identification "in the relevant Confirmation," yet Paragraph 3(a) permits oral agreement and Paragraph 3(b) leaves who delivers a Confirmation to agreement, so an unclassified trade's status is unresolved. A modest coherence question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive documentation rule allowing one or two Confirmations. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with Paragraph 3(b) and Annex VI paragraph 5's Pricing Rate recording requirement. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two sentences describe overlapping accrual periods, the first running to the date of calculation and the second to the next Income payment or maturity date, which is confusing on its face. The intent is recoverable but the drafting is doubled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses the Agreement's "Income" definition and feeds Annex VI paragraph 7's Purchase Price and Sell Back Price adjustments. Consistent in use.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise daily-accrual formula parallel to Paragraph 2(k), with an express opt-out from the 360-day convention. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds the Sell Back Price formula in 4(c)(ii) and is consistent with Paragraph 2(k)'s Price Differential. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-limb definition, the second an algebraic formula with defined variables; the OCR renders "the product of the formula (P + D) - (IR + C)" although the expression is a difference, not a product. That mismatch between the words and the symbols is a mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is invoked "for the purposes of the application of Paragraph 4 or Paragraph 11 of the Agreement" and is reinforced by Annex VI paragraphs 10 and 11's construction directives. Coherent with those.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short mandatory obligations about agreeing and recording terms. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplements Paragraph 3(b)'s Confirmation contents without contradiction. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A termination mechanic distinguishing the originally agreed Repurchase Date from any other case, each routed to a specific definition. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels Paragraph 3(c) for Buy/Sell Back Transactions and coordinates with Paragraph 2(q). No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The whole rule is subject to "except to the extent contrary to market practice with respect to the Securities," an unfixed external standard that switches the parties into an entirely different formula. That switch turns on a contestable factual standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It rewrites the 4(c)(ii) formula and interacts with 4(a) Accrued Interest and Paragraph 2(o)'s Purchase Price; the substitution is stated expressly. Reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It presupposes a repricing regime ("at the time of repricing") that the Agreement nowhere establishes, and the opt-out is located in an Annex I that says nothing about repricing. The unanchored reference is a real gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I contains no Buy/Sell Back repricing election, so the default is an obligation to agree terms at an event the instrument never defines. That incompleteness is confined to the Buy/Sell Back annex.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short sentences: Paragraph 5 is disapplied and Income flows from Seller to Buyer instead. The words themselves are plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely reverses Paragraph 5 and cannot be reconciled with Annex I paragraph 3, which mandates that Buyer transfer Income to Seller under Paragraph 5(i) "in any Transaction hereunder" — and Annex I paragraph 2 and Annex VI paragraph 1 each claim precedence over the other. That is a genuine, unranked conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A sweeping construction directive rewriting a defined term "throughout the Agreement" as "Repurchase Price or the Sell Back Price, as the case may be," with no indication of how to tell which case is which. The phrase "as the case may be" carries all the work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Applied literally it alters Paragraphs 2(c), 2(s), 4(e), 11(b), 11(e) and 11(f) even for ordinary Repurchase Transactions, which the parties presumably did not intend. Paragraph 11 also gets a separate, narrower directive in Annex VI paragraph 11, raising the question why both were needed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence opens "In 11 of the Agreement," omitting the word "Paragraph," and duplicates the broader directive in the immediately preceding paragraph. Both the omission and the redundancy are visible on the face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Annex VI paragraph 10, which already covers every reference throughout the Agreement including Paragraph 11, leaving the narrower rule with no independent work. A redundancy rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital defines the parties as Barclays and "each investment company identified on Schedule VII.A," and embeds a precedence rule using the undefined trigger "any conflict." The definitional chain depends on a schedule that was left blank.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: As adopted by Annex I paragraph 1, this annex purports to substitute unnamed Funds for Thornburg as counterparty and to prevail over "any other term of the Agreement," competing with Annex I paragraph 2 and Annex VI paragraph 1 for primacy. Reading it into a two-party principal deal produces genuine incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The per-Fund ring-fencing is expressed clearly with three specific illustrations. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disapplies Paragraph 12's single-agreement and set-off provisions across Funds and overrides Paragraph 4 aggregation, all expressly; but it does so in an annex made applicable to a deal with no identified Funds. The override is stated, so the incoherence is one of applicability.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The percentage is left blank ("equal to at least _%"), and the second sentence, addressed to a Fund acting as Seller, still speaks only of the Buyer's Margin Percentage — a blank plus an apparent drafting slip in the same short paragraph. Both defects are visible on the face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides Paragraph 2(d)'s and 2(t)'s default margin-percentage formulas with a 100% floor for any Fund Transaction, and Annex I paragraph 1 makes the annex applicable even though Schedule VII.A identifies no Fund. The blank and the floor cannot both be given effect coherently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short obligations to issue Confirmations and transfer notices, qualified only by "[u]nless otherwise agreed" and "promptly." Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It allocates the Paragraph 3(b) Confirmation duty to Counterparty, which Paragraph 3(b) leaves to agreement — a supplement rather than a conflict. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A representation about financial information delivered, with the applicable category keyed to specific SEC and Investment Company Act rules. Precise in its references.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels Paragraph 18(b)-(c)'s financial-statement regime for plan Transactions without contradicting it, and its breach would feed Paragraph 11(vi). Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete delivery mechanic routed through a designated Custodian, with a special case where the transferor is itself the Custodian. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on a Custodian "designated for such Fund in Schedule VII.A," and that schedule is entirely blank, so the mechanic has no referent; it also sits alongside Paragraph 8's segregation rule. The dependency on an unfilled schedule is the weak point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision consists of an introductory sentence followed by empty "Name of Fund" and "Custodian" columns, so it identifies nothing. An unexecuted schedule is a defect visible on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex VII, Annex VII paragraph 5 and Annex VII paragraph 2 all depend on this schedule, and Annex I paragraph 1 nonetheless lists it as forming part of the Agreement. Making an empty schedule operative is a coherence problem for the instrument as a whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is an unfilled template: "[insert appropriate language limiting liability of trustees, officers and others]." There is no operative text at all, which is the plainest form of mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is made part of the Agreement by Annex I paragraph 1 even though no Fund, still less a business trust, is identified on Schedule VII.A, so the condition for its operation can never be met. Its emptiness leaves nothing to conflict with elsewhere.
